minutes.headline: Board voted to study installing a small lift to reach unused upstairs rooms at Eagle House.
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging approved its FY26 minutes and officer slate, heard tributes to two retiring longtime members, and reviewed FY27 budget plans including a possible full-time recreation director and new outreach/program-coordinator roles. Most of the meeting was spent debating building furniture and space use, a proposed capital study for a lift to unused upstairs rooms (approved by motion), and a contested plan to extend building hours, which the board agreed to trial rather than vote on outright.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes with the correction (fixing a typo).
Approve Debbie and Jane for the officer slate for the coming year.
Do a study (architectural/feasibility) toward installing a lift for the upstairs rooms.

budget_items.what_was_said: The director said the main FY27 change on the radar is shifting a position toward an assistant-director-of-outreach role and adding a program coordinator.
The chair noted the programs line needs watching because it sees large incremental increases each year, and costs will rise a bit across the board in FY27.
The Town Manager said one area of proposed FY27 growth is making the recreation director a full-time position, with funding and structure still to be worked out.
The director explained meals run through a revolving account with no dedicated fund source, and proposed adding a buffer so a shortfall between what a meal costs and what is collected is covered.
The director presented the May Munis report and a simplified spreadsheet showing the department's town-meeting-awarded funds are essentially used up heading into July 1.
The director said she requested QuickBooks, not yet approved, to track the department's funds in-house and compare against the town's records.
A board member recalled a past building project quoted at roughly this figure, offered as a cost comparison for the proposed lift.
The Town Manager cited a vendor's published average cost for a two-stop lift installation in a public building, plus an ongoing inspection cost.
A member of the public described a similar ongoing local lift project and cited a received quote for a two-person unit, calling it all-inclusive with engineering and permitting.
Eagle House Supporters described an in-store fundraising bag program at Hannaford where purchasing the correct bag contributes to the group's fundraising.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to let a member investigate and bring back a fuller proposal on building-permit protections for senior home repairs at a future meeting.
Rather than adopt either the couches or the library-style chairs, the board agreed to look for a compromise furniture option for the entry seating area.
Hold off finalizing the kiosk print materials until the new building hours are settled.
Trial the proposed increase in building hours (adding evening hours, reducing some Friday hours) through at least September before evaluating, rather than a straight vote.

what_happened.line: Board voted to commission a feasibility study for a lift to reach unused upstairs rooms at Eagle House.
Board agreed to trial extended building hours -- more evenings, fewer Friday afternoons -- through at least September rather than vote on it outright.
FY27 budget planning flagged a possible full-time recreation director and new outreach and program-coordinator roles.
Board postponed a decision on entry-seating furniture, agreeing to look for a compromise between two options.
Board approved its officer slate for the coming year and thanked two retiring longtime members.

why_it_matters: A capital study for an elevator or lift is a step toward a construction project that would need town funding and a building-committee process before any work happens.
A trial of building hours changes when seniors can use Eagle House's programs and services, ahead of any permanent change.
Proposed new staff roles and a full-time recreation director would show up as line items in the FY27 town budget residents vote on at town meeting.
watch_next: Results of the lift feasibility/architectural study
Evaluation of the extended-hours trial after September, and the FY27 budget proposal

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the officer election, the lift study vote, the permit research and the kiosk hold, but they differ on the furniture decision, the length of the hours trial and the lift cost figures. A reader should check the recording on the Bucky's Corner furniture: ours records a board agreement to seek a compromise, while the official minutes record only the Town Manager's suggestion.
